passage: In the dry interior of Australia, rain may not fall for many months. The water-holding frog survives these long droughts underground. After a heavy rain, the frog stores extra water in its body and then burrows into the soil. There it sheds several layers of skin, which harden around it into a snug cocoon that slows the loss of moisture. Sealed inside, the frog can wait for months, sometimes far longer, until the next heavy rain softens the ground and it digs its way back to the surface.
stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
option_a: To describe how one animal survives long periods without rain
option_b: To compare the water-holding frog with other desert animals
option_c: To explain why rain is so rare in the interior of Australia
option_d: To argue that the water-holding frog is threatened by climate change
explanation_en:
Nearly every sentence describes the steps the frog takes to get through a drought: storing water, burrowing, forming a cocoon, and waiting for rain. Choice A states this purpose.

Choice B is wrong because no other animals are mentioned. Choice C is wrong because the text only notes that rain is rare; it never explains why. Choice D is wrong because climate change and threats to the frog are not discussed.
explanation_uz:
Deyarli har bir gap qurbaqaning qurg‘oqchilikdan qanday omon qolishini bosqichma-bosqich tasvirlaydi: suv to‘plash, yerga ko‘milish, pilla hosil qilish va yomg‘irni kutish. A javob aynan shu maqsadni ifodalaydi.

B noto‘g‘ri: boshqa hayvonlar tilga olinmagan. C noto‘g‘ri: matn faqat yomg‘ir kam yog‘ishini qayd etadi, sababini tushuntirmaydi. D noto‘g‘ri: iqlim o‘zgarishi yoki qurbaqaga tahdidlar muhokama qilinmaydi.

passage: Along the old trade routes of Central Asia, travelers rested at caravanserais, walled inns built around a large open courtyard. These inns were usually spaced about a day's journey apart, so that a caravan setting out at dawn could reach the next one before dark. The single, heavy gate could be locked at night to protect travelers and their goods, and the courtyard held enough space for dozens of camels, while rooms for the merchants lined the surrounding walls.
stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
option_a: To argue that caravanserais were more comfortable than modern hotels
option_b: To explain why trade along Central Asian routes declined
option_c: To tell the story of a particular caravan's journey
option_d: To describe how the design and placement of caravanserais served the needs of travelers
explanation_en:
The text explains that caravanserais were spaced a day's journey apart so caravans could arrive before dark, had a lockable gate for safety, and had room for camels and merchants. Each detail links a feature of the inns to a traveler's need, as choice D says.

Choice A is wrong because modern hotels are never mentioned. Choice B is wrong because the text says nothing about trade declining. Choice C is wrong because the text describes caravanserais in general, not one specific caravan's trip.
explanation_uz:
Matnda karvonsaroylar karvon qorong‘i tushguncha yetib olishi uchun bir kunlik yo‘l oralig‘ida qurilgani, xavfsizlik uchun qulflanadigan darvozasi va tuyalar hamda savdogarlar uchun joyi borligi tushuntiriladi. Har bir tafsilot binoning biror xususiyatini yo‘lovchilarning ehtiyoji bilan bog‘laydi — D javobda aytilganidek.

A noto‘g‘ri: zamonaviy mehmonxonalar tilga olinmagan. B noto‘g‘ri: savdoning pasayishi haqida hech narsa aytilmagan. C noto‘g‘ri: matn muayyan bir karvonning safarini emas, umuman karvonsaroylarni tasvirlaydi.

passage: When the public library in the city of Nurafshon began staying open until 10 p.m., librarians expected the extra hours to attract mostly students preparing for exams. Instead, the evening visitors turned out to be remarkably varied. __On a typical night, a nurse coming off a late shift might be reading in one corner while a retired engineer helped a group of children with their science projects in another.__ The library's director now describes the evening hours as the busiest and most mixed of the day.
stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
option_a: It explains why librarians first decided to extend the library's hours.
option_b: It gives an example of the variety of people who use the library in the evening.
option_c: It presents evidence that most evening visitors are students preparing for exams.
option_d: It describes a problem that the library's director hopes to solve.
explanation_en:
The sentence before the underlined one says the evening visitors were “remarkably varied.” The underlined sentence then shows this variety with specific people: a nurse, a retired engineer, and children. It is an example, as choice B says.

Choice A is wrong because the sentence does not explain the decision to extend hours. Choice C is wrong because the text says the librarians' expectation about students was wrong, and the sentence mentions no exam students. Choice D is wrong because the sentence describes a positive situation, not a problem.
explanation_uz:
Belgilangan gapdan oldingi gapda kechki tashrif buyuruvchilar “juda xilma-xil” ekani aytiladi. Belgilangan gap esa bu xilma-xillikni aniq odamlar orqali ko‘rsatadi: hamshira, nafaqadagi muhandis va bolalar. Bu — misol, B javobda aytilganidek.

A noto‘g‘ri: gap ish vaqtini uzaytirish qarorini tushuntirmaydi. C noto‘g‘ri: matnga ko‘ra kutubxonachilarning talabalar haqidagi taxmini noto‘g‘ri chiqqan, gapda imtihonga tayyorlanayotgan talabalar tilga olinmaydi. D noto‘g‘ri: gap muammoni emas, ijobiy holatni tasvirlaydi.

passage:
The following text is from a short story. Zarina is about to perform in her first piano competition.

Zarina sat in the wings with her hands pressed flat against her knees to keep them still. Out on the stage, the boy before her was finishing his piece, and every note he played seemed to her more perfect than anything she could manage. She went over the opening bars of her own piece in her head, then went over them again, and then could not remember whether the third chord came before or after the long rest.
stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
option_a: To describe the boy who performs before Zarina
option_b: To explain how Zarina chose the piece she will perform
option_c: To show Zarina's nervousness as she waits to perform
option_d: To suggest that Zarina is confident she will win the competition
explanation_en:
Zarina presses her hands against her knees “to keep them still,” thinks the other boy's playing is better than hers, rehearses her opening again and again, and then forgets part of it. These details show her anxiety before performing, as choice C says.

Choice A is wrong because the boy is mentioned only to show how Zarina reacts to him. Choice B is wrong because the text never explains how she chose her piece. Choice D is wrong because she doubts herself; nothing suggests confidence.
explanation_uz:
Zarina qo‘llari qimirlamasligi uchun ularni tizzalariga bosib turadi, boshqa bolaning chalishi o‘zinikidan yaxshiroq deb o‘ylaydi, asarining boshlanishini qayta-qayta takrorlaydi va oxiri uning bir qismini unutib qo‘yadi. Bu tafsilotlar uning chiqish oldidan hayajonlanayotganini ko‘rsatadi — C javob.

A noto‘g‘ri: bola faqat Zarinaning unga munosabatini ko‘rsatish uchun tilga olinadi. B noto‘g‘ri: matnda u asarni qanday tanlagani aytilmaydi. D noto‘g‘ri: u o‘ziga ishonmaydi, ishonch haqida hech qanday ishora yo‘q.

passage: Many people believe that a camel's hump is filled with water. In fact, the hump stores fat, which the camel can draw on for energy when food is scarce. Camels survive long stretches without drinking for other reasons. Their bodies lose very little water through sweat and urine, and they can tolerate a degree of dehydration that would kill most other mammals. When they finally reach water, they can drink enormous amounts in just a few minutes.
stem: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
option_a: It describes how camels find water and then explains how they store it in their humps.
option_b: It compares camels with other mammals and then argues that camels are the best-adapted desert animals.
option_c: It presents a common belief about camels, corrects it, and then gives the actual reasons camels can go long periods without drinking.
option_d: It lists several features of camels and then explains how scientists discovered each one.
explanation_en:
The text opens with a belief (“Many people believe” the hump holds water), corrects it (“In fact, the hump stores fat”), and then explains the real reasons camels can go without drinking. Choice C describes this structure.

Choice A is wrong because the text denies that camels store water in their humps. Choice B is wrong because other mammals are mentioned only briefly, and the text never claims camels are the best-adapted desert animals. Choice D is wrong because the text never describes how scientists made any discoveries.
explanation_uz:
Matn bir qarash bilan boshlanadi (“Ko‘pchilik o‘rkachda suv bor deb hisoblaydi”), so‘ng uni tuzatadi (“Aslida o‘rkachda yog‘ saqlanadi”) va keyin tuyalar uzoq vaqt suv ichmasdan yura olishining haqiqiy sabablarini tushuntiradi. C javob shu tuzilishni tasvirlaydi.

A noto‘g‘ri: matn tuya o‘rkachida suv saqlashini rad etadi. B noto‘g‘ri: boshqa sutemizuvchilar faqat qisqa tilga olinadi va tuyalar cho‘lga eng yaxshi moslashgan hayvon deb da’vo qilinmaydi. D noto‘g‘ri: matnda olimlar biror narsani qanday kashf etgani tasvirlanmaydi.

passage: In Uzbekistan, large embroidered textiles called suzani were traditionally made by the women of a bride's family as part of her dowry. Because a single suzani could take months or even years to complete, the cloth was often cut into several long strips, and each strip was embroidered by a different relative before the pieces were sewn back together. __As a result, the patterns on neighboring strips do not always line up perfectly, and the colors of a single flower may shift slightly from one strip to the next.__
stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
option_a: It describes a visible effect of the way suzani were made.
option_b: It explains why suzani took so long to complete.
option_c: It argues that suzani made by a single person are more valuable.
option_d: It suggests that the women who made suzani lacked skill.
explanation_en:
The previous sentence explains that each strip was embroidered by a different relative and then sewn together. The underlined sentence, starting with “As a result,” describes what this produces: patterns that do not line up and colors that shift. It describes an effect of the process, as choice A says.

Choice B is wrong because the length of the work is explained in the previous sentence, not in the underlined one. Choice C is wrong because the text never compares the value of different suzani. Choice D is wrong because the mismatches come from several people working separately, not from a lack of skill.
explanation_uz:
Oldingi gapda har bir bo‘lakni boshqa qarindosh tikkani va keyin bo‘laklar birlashtirilgani tushuntiriladi. “As a result” (natijada) bilan boshlanadigan belgilangan gap bu jarayonning oqibatini tasvirlaydi: naqshlar bir-biriga to‘liq mos kelmaydi, ranglar biroz farq qiladi. Demak, gap tayyorlash usulining ko‘zga ko‘rinadigan natijasini tasvirlaydi — A javob.

B noto‘g‘ri: ishning uzoq davom etishi belgilangan gapda emas, oldingi gapda tushuntirilgan. C noto‘g‘ri: matnda turli suzanalarning qiymati taqqoslanmaydi. D noto‘g‘ri: nomuvofiqliklar mahorat yetishmasligidan emas, bir necha kishi alohida ishlaganidan kelib chiqadi.

passage: Birds that live in cities often sing at a higher pitch than members of the same species living in forests. Biologist Rustam Qosimov assumed that the birds were simply avoiding the low rumble of traffic, which can drown out deep notes. To test this idea, he recorded birds in quiet city parks far from busy roads. Surprisingly, these birds also sang at high pitches. Qosimov now suspects that hard surfaces such as glass and concrete, which reflect high notes more clearly than low ones, may also shape urban birdsong.
stem: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
option_a: It describes a difference in birdsong, explains why traffic noise is harmful to birds, and then recommends quieter roads.
option_b: It notes a pattern in birdsong, presents a researcher's explanation and a test of it, and then describes how an unexpected result led him to consider another factor.
option_c: It presents two competing explanations for a pattern in birdsong and then describes an experiment showing that both are wrong.
option_d: It describes how a researcher recorded birdsong and then explains why city birds sing more often than forest birds.
explanation_en:
The text first notes a pattern (city birds sing at higher pitches), then gives Qosimov's explanation (avoiding traffic noise) and his test of it (recording in quiet parks). The “surprising” result leads him to suspect another factor, reflective surfaces. Choice B follows this order.

Choice A is wrong because the text never recommends quieter roads or discusses harm to birds. Choice C is wrong because the text begins with only one explanation, and the result does not show both explanations are wrong; Qosimov thinks surfaces “may also” play a role. Choice D is wrong because the text is about pitch, not how often birds sing.
explanation_uz:
Matn avval bir qonuniyatni qayd etadi (shahar qushlari balandroq ovozda sayraydi), keyin Qosimovning izohini (transport shovqinidan qochish) va uni sinovdan o‘tkazishini (tinch bog‘larda yozib olish) keltiradi. “Kutilmagan” natija uni boshqa omil — aks ettiruvchi sirtlar haqida o‘ylashga undaydi. B javob shu tartibga mos.

A noto‘g‘ri: matnda tinchroq yo‘llar taklif qilinmaydi va qushlarga zarar muhokama qilinmaydi. C noto‘g‘ri: matn faqat bitta izoh bilan boshlanadi va natija ikkala izoh ham noto‘g‘ri ekanini ko‘rsatmaydi — Qosimov sirtlar “ham” ta’sir qilishi mumkin deb hisoblaydi. D noto‘g‘ri: matn qushlar qanchalik tez-tez sayrashi haqida emas, ovoz balandligi haqida.

passage: In 2021, the city of Yangiobod made its buses free to ride. Over the next two years, the number of bus trips rose by 38 percent, and economist Dilshod Ergashev argues that eliminating fares was the main reason. __Ridership did also rise in two nearby cities that kept their fares, though by only about 10 percent, probably because of new housing built along their bus routes.__ Even so, Ergashev notes, Yangiobod's increase was nearly four times as large, a gap that new housing alone cannot easily explain.
stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
option_a: It provides the main evidence for Ergashev's claim that free fares increased ridership.
option_b: It explains why Yangiobod decided to stop charging bus fares.
option_c: It suggests that Ergashev's conclusion about Yangiobod is mistaken.
option_d: It acknowledges a fact that might seem to weaken Ergashev's claim before the text explains why that claim still holds.
explanation_en:
Ergashev claims that free fares were the main cause of Yangiobod's ridership increase. The underlined sentence admits that ridership rose even in cities that kept fares, which might suggest other causes. The next sentence (“Even so”) explains that Yangiobod's increase was much larger. So the underlined sentence concedes a complicating fact, as choice D says.

Choice A is wrong because ridership growth in other cities does not support the free-fare explanation; the main evidence is the 38 percent rise and the comparison that follows. Choice B is wrong because the sentence is about other cities, not about Yangiobod's decision. Choice C is wrong because the text goes on to defend Ergashev's conclusion rather than reject it.
explanation_uz:
Ergashev Yangiobodda yo‘lovchilar ko‘payishining asosiy sababi bepul yo‘l haqi deb hisoblaydi. Belgilangan gap esa yo‘l haqini saqlab qolgan shaharlarda ham yo‘lovchilar ko‘payganini tan oladi — bu boshqa sabablar ham bor degan fikrga olib kelishi mumkin. Keyingi gap (“Even so” — shunday bo‘lsa-da) Yangiobodda o‘sish ancha katta bo‘lganini tushuntiradi. Demak, belgilangan gap da’voni murakkablashtiruvchi faktni tan oladi — D javob.

A noto‘g‘ri: boshqa shaharlardagi o‘sish bepul yo‘l haqi izohini qo‘llab-quvvatlamaydi; asosiy dalil — 38 foizlik o‘sish va undan keyingi taqqoslash. B noto‘g‘ri: gap Yangiobodning qarori haqida emas, boshqa shaharlar haqida. C noto‘g‘ri: matn keyin Ergashevning xulosasini rad etmaydi, balki himoya qiladi.

passage: In the 1890s, Mariam Valieva was one of only a handful of women working as professional photographers in the Russian Empire, yet her name rarely appears in histories of the period. Historian Gulnora Saidova argues that this neglect has little to do with the quality of Valieva's work. Most of Valieva's surviving prints, Saidova points out, were stamped with the name of the studio that employed her rather than her own, so for decades archivists simply credited them to the studio's male owner.
stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
option_a: To present a historian's explanation for why a photographer's work has been overlooked
option_b: To argue that Valieva was the most talented photographer of her time
option_c: To describe the techniques Valieva used to produce her photographs
option_d: To criticize archivists for deliberately hiding the work of women photographers
explanation_en:
The text notes that Valieva is rarely mentioned in histories and then presents Saidova's explanation: her prints were stamped with the studio's name, so archivists credited them to the studio's owner. Choice A captures this purpose.

Choice B is wrong because the text says the neglect is not about quality but never claims Valieva was the most talented. Choice C is wrong because no photographic techniques are described. Choice D is wrong because the archivists credited the studio owner “simply” because of the stamp; the text does not say they acted deliberately, and its tone is explanatory rather than critical.
explanation_uz:
Matnda Valieva tarix kitoblarida kam tilga olinishi qayd etiladi, so‘ng Saidovaning izohi keltiriladi: suratlarga studiya nomi muhrlangani sababli arxivchilar ularni studiya egasiga nisbat bergan. A javob shu maqsadni ifodalaydi.

B noto‘g‘ri: matnda e’tibordan chetda qolish sifat bilan bog‘liq emasligi aytiladi, ammo Valieva o‘z davrining eng iste’dodli fotografi deb da’vo qilinmaydi. C noto‘g‘ri: fotosurat texnikalari tasvirlanmagan. D noto‘g‘ri: arxivchilar muhr sababli “shunchaki” studiya egasini ko‘rsatgan; ular buni ataylab qilgani aytilmaydi, matn ohangi esa tanqidiy emas, tushuntiruvchi.

passage:
The following text is from a short story. Akmal has returned to his family's farm after several years working in the city.

His father met him at the gate and took his suitcase without a word, as he always had. They walked up the path together past the apricot trees. Akmal noticed that the fence by the well had been mended with new wire, and that the old dog no longer came running. __He wanted to ask about the dog, but his father was already talking about the price of seed, and the moment passed.__ Inside, his mother had set the table for three.
stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
option_a: It shows that Akmal has forgotten the details of life on the farm.
option_b: It conveys Akmal's hesitation to raise a painful question and the ease with which the chance to ask it slips away.
option_c: It reveals that Akmal's father is angry that his son left the farm.
option_d: It explains why the fence by the well had to be repaired.
explanation_en:
Akmal notices that the old dog “no longer came running,” suggesting the dog may have died. In the underlined sentence he wants to ask about it but does not, and “the moment passed” while his father talks about something ordinary. The sentence conveys his reluctance to raise a painful topic and how easily the chance slips by, as choice B says.

Choice A is wrong because Akmal notices small changes on the farm, which shows he remembers it well. Choice C is wrong because the father's silence and talk about seed prices are presented as his usual manner (“as he always had”), not as anger. Choice D is wrong because the sentence is about the dog, not the fence.
explanation_uz:
Akmal keksa it endi “yugurib chiqmayotgani”ni payqaydi — bu it o‘lgan bo‘lishi mumkinligiga ishora. Belgilangan gapda u bu haqda so‘ramoqchi bo‘ladi, lekin otasi oddiy narsa haqida gapirayotganda “fursat o‘tib ketadi”. Gap Akmalning og‘riqli savolni berishga ikkilanishini va bu imkoniyat qanchalik oson qo‘ldan chiqishini ifodalaydi — B javob.

A noto‘g‘ri: Akmal fermadagi kichik o‘zgarishlarni payqaydi, demak uni yaxshi eslaydi. C noto‘g‘ri: otaning jimligi va urug‘ narxi haqidagi gapi uning odatiy xulqi sifatida berilgan (“as he always had”), g‘azab sifatida emas. D noto‘g‘ri: gap to‘siq haqida emas, it haqida.

passage: Merchant account books from the Black Sea port of Seravan, kept in the 1460s, are mostly long columns of prices and quantities that few historians had studied closely. When historian Anvar Tojiboyev examined the originals rather than printed copies, he noticed that dozens of entries for grain had been scraped away and rewritten, always with higher prices. By comparing these corrections with records of storms and blockades, Tojiboyev concluded that the merchants had revised their accounts during sudden shortages, revealing how quickly grain prices responded to crises at sea.
stem: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
option_a: It argues that printed copies of historical documents are unreliable and then recommends that historians avoid them.
option_b: It describes a storm that struck a port and then explains how merchants responded to it.
option_c: It explains how account books were kept and then compares the prices of several goods.
option_d: It introduces a type of source that has received little attention, describes a feature one historian noticed in it, and explains what he learned from that feature.
explanation_en:
The text first introduces the account books, which “few historians had studied closely.” It then describes what Tojiboyev noticed (scraped and rewritten grain prices) and finally explains what he concluded about how prices responded to crises. Choice D matches this sequence.

Choice A is wrong because the text never argues that printed copies are unreliable in general or recommends avoiding them; it only notes that Tojiboyev looked at the originals. Choice B is wrong because no single storm is described; storms are mentioned only as records Tojiboyev compared. Choice C is wrong because the text discusses only grain prices and does not explain how the books were kept.
explanation_uz:
Matn avval hisob daftarlarini tanishtiradi — ularni “kam tarixchi sinchiklab o‘rgangan”. Keyin Tojiboyev nimani payqaganini (don narxlari qirib tashlanib, qayta yozilganini) tasvirlaydi va oxirida narxlar inqirozlarga qanday javob bergani haqidagi xulosasini tushuntiradi. D javob shu ketma-ketlikka mos.

A noto‘g‘ri: matnda bosma nusxalar umuman ishonchsiz deb da’vo qilinmaydi va ulardan voz kechish tavsiya etilmaydi; faqat Tojiboyev asl nusxalarni ko‘rgani aytiladi. B noto‘g‘ri: muayyan bir bo‘ron tasvirlanmagan; bo‘ronlar faqat Tojiboyev taqqoslagan yozuvlar sifatida tilga olinadi. C noto‘g‘ri: matnda faqat don narxlari muhokama qilinadi va daftarlar qanday yuritilgani tushuntirilmaydi.

passage: In regions with distinct seasons, most trees add one growth ring each year, and the width of each ring depends on that year's weather: wet years generally produce wide rings, and dry years narrow ones. Because the pattern of wide and narrow rings over several decades is unlikely to repeat exactly, researchers can match the pattern in an old wooden beam with the overlapping pattern in a living tree or another dated timber. Linking many such overlapping sequences allows them to determine the year in which a beam's tree was cut down.
stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
option_a: To argue that tree rings are the most accurate source of information about past weather
option_b: To describe how weather in wet years differs from weather in dry years
option_c: To explain how patterns in tree rings can be used to date old pieces of wood
option_d: To compare the growth of trees in regions with and without distinct seasons
explanation_en:
The text explains that ring widths vary with weather, that ring patterns over decades are distinctive, and that matching overlapping patterns lets researchers date a beam. Every sentence builds toward explaining this dating method, as choice C says.

Choice A is wrong because the text does not compare tree rings with other sources or call them the most accurate. Choice B is wrong because wet and dry years are mentioned only to explain why rings differ in width. Choice D is wrong because regions without distinct seasons are never discussed.
explanation_uz:
Matnda halqalar kengligi ob-havoga qarab o‘zgarishi, o‘n yilliklar davomidagi halqa naqshi o‘ziga xos bo‘lishi va bir-birini qoplaydigan naqshlarni moslashtirib, to‘sin yoshini aniqlash mumkinligi tushuntiriladi. Har bir gap shu sanalash usulini tushuntirishga xizmat qiladi — C javob.

A noto‘g‘ri: matnda daraxt halqalari boshqa manbalar bilan taqqoslanmaydi va eng aniq manba deyilmaydi. B noto‘g‘ri: nam va quruq yillar faqat halqalar kengligi nega farq qilishini tushuntirish uchun tilga olinadi. D noto‘g‘ri: aniq fasllari bo‘lmagan mintaqalar muhokama qilinmaydi.

passage:
The following text is from a short story. Nilufar has returned to the village where she grew up.

The street was narrower than she remembered, and the great plane tree in the square, which had once seemed to hold up the whole sky, was only a tree. The teahouse where her grandfather had argued about politics every evening now sold mobile phone cards. She felt foolish for having expected anything else. Still, when an old woman at the well squinted at her and said, “You're Hamid's granddaughter, aren't you? You have his frown,” Nilufar found that she had to look away for a moment.
stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
option_a: To show that Nilufar is relieved to find that the village has modernized
option_b: To describe the changes in the village in order to criticize its residents for abandoning tradition
option_c: To explain why Nilufar left the village when she was young
option_d: To convey Nilufar's mixed feelings as she finds the village diminished yet discovers that she is still recognized as belonging to it
explanation_en:
The first part of the text stresses disappointment: the street is “narrower,” the tree is “only a tree,” the teahouse has changed, and Nilufar feels “foolish.” Then “Still” introduces a turn: an old woman recognizes her as Hamid's granddaughter, and Nilufar is so moved that she must look away. The text conveys both feelings at once, as choice D says.

Choice A is wrong because Nilufar feels foolish and let down by the changes, not relieved. Choice B is wrong because the changes are described from Nilufar's point of view without blaming the residents. Choice C is wrong because the text never says why she left.
explanation_uz:
Matnning birinchi qismi hafsalasi pir bo‘lganini ta’kidlaydi: ko‘cha “torroq”, chinor “shunchaki daraxt”, choyxona o‘zgargan, Nilufar esa o‘zini “ahmoqona” his qiladi. Keyin “Still” (shunday bo‘lsa-da) burilishni boshlaydi: keksa ayol uni Hamidning nabirasi deb taniydi va Nilufar shunchalik ta’sirlanadiki, bir lahza ko‘zini olib qochadi. Matn ikkala tuyg‘uni birga ifodalaydi — D javob.

A noto‘g‘ri: Nilufar o‘zgarishlardan yengil tortmaydi, aksincha hafsalasi pir bo‘ladi. B noto‘g‘ri: o‘zgarishlar Nilufar nigohi orqali tasvirlanadi, aholi ayblanmaydi. C noto‘g‘ri: matnda uning nega ketgani aytilmaydi.

passage: Lichens, partnerships between a fungus and an alga or bacterium, are often called pioneer organisms because they can grow on bare rock where nothing else lives. Over centuries, acids they release help break the rock into the first thin layers of soil. __This is not to say that every patch of bare rock must wait for lichens before plants can take hold: on some lava flows, ecologists have found mosses and even ferns rooted in cracks where windblown dust had collected, with no lichens nearby.__ In most rocky landscapes, though, lichens remain among the first arrivals.
stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
option_a: It qualifies the claim that lichens are pioneer organisms by noting cases in which plants became established without them.
option_b: It provides additional evidence that lichens are necessary for soil to form on bare rock.
option_c: It explains how lichens produce the acids that break down rock.
option_d: It rejects the view that lichens contribute to soil formation.
explanation_en:
The text presents lichens as pioneers that prepare bare rock for later life. The underlined sentence, beginning “This is not to say,” limits that idea: on some lava flows, plants grew without lichens. The final sentence then reaffirms that lichens are usually among the first arrivals. So the underlined sentence qualifies, rather than rejects, the main claim, as choice A says.

Choice B is wrong because the example shows plants growing without lichens, which goes against the idea that lichens are always necessary. Choice C is wrong because the acids are mentioned in the previous sentence, and the underlined sentence does not explain them. Choice D is too extreme: the sentence notes exceptions, and the text still says lichens help form soil and are usually first.
explanation_uz:
Matn lishayniklarni yalang‘och toshni keyingi hayot uchun tayyorlaydigan “kashshof” organizmlar sifatida taqdim etadi. “This is not to say” (bu degani emas) bilan boshlanadigan belgilangan gap bu fikrni cheklaydi: ba’zi lava oqimlarida o‘simliklar lishayniklarsiz o‘sgan. Oxirgi gap esa lishayniklar odatda birinchilar qatorida ekanini yana tasdiqlaydi. Demak, belgilangan gap asosiy da’voni rad etmaydi, balki uni aniqlashtirib, chegaralaydi — A javob.

B noto‘g‘ri: misol o‘simliklar lishayniksiz o‘sganini ko‘rsatadi, ya’ni lishayniklar har doim zarur degan fikrga zid. C noto‘g‘ri: kislotalar oldingi gapda tilga olingan, belgilangan gap ularni tushuntirmaydi. D juda keskin: gap faqat istisnolarni qayd etadi, matn esa baribir lishayniklar tuproq hosil bo‘lishiga yordam beradi va odatda birinchi keladi deydi.

passage: Scholars have long agreed that the poet Gulruh Sobiri, who wrote in the early nineteenth century, drew heavily on the Persian lyric tradition, borrowing its images of the nightingale and the rose. Literary historian Barno Ahmedova accepts this view but argues that it tells only half the story. In several of Sobiri's poems, Ahmedova observes, these familiar images appear alongside references to local places and events, such as the gardens of Kokand and a specific flood, details that would have meant little to readers outside the region. The borrowed images, she suggests, were reshaped to speak to a particular local audience.
stem: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
option_a: It presents a researcher's new interpretation of a poet's work and then describes the established view that this interpretation replaced.
option_b: It describes an established view of a poet's influences, presents a researcher who accepts that view but adds to it, and gives the evidence for her addition.
option_c: It describes a disagreement between two scholars and then explains why neither scholar's view is supported by the poems.
option_d: It summarizes a poet's life and then lists the images that appear most often in her work.
explanation_en:
The text begins with what scholars “have long agreed” on: Sobiri drew on Persian traditions. It then introduces Ahmedova, who “accepts this view” but says it is only “half the story,” and offers evidence (local places and events in the poems) for her addition. Choice B describes this structure in the correct order.

Choice A reverses the order and misstates the relationship: the established view comes first, and Ahmedova adds to it rather than replacing it. Choice C is wrong because Ahmedova does not disagree with the earlier scholars, and the text supports her view with evidence from the poems. Choice D is wrong because the text gives no biography of Sobiri and does not simply list images.
explanation_uz:
Matn olimlar “uzoq vaqtdan beri kelishgan” fikr bilan boshlanadi: Sobiri fors lirik an’analariga tayangan. Keyin bu qarashni “qabul qiladigan”, ammo u “hikoyaning yarmi, xolos” deydigan Ahmedova tanishtiriladi va uning qo‘shimchasi uchun dalil (she’rlardagi mahalliy joylar va voqealar) keltiriladi. B javob bu tuzilishni to‘g‘ri tartibda tasvirlaydi.

A tartibni teskari qiladi va munosabatni noto‘g‘ri beradi: avval eski qarash keladi, Ahmedova esa uni almashtirmaydi, balki to‘ldiradi. C noto‘g‘ri: Ahmedova avvalgi olimlarga qarshi chiqmaydi va matn uning fikrini she’rlardan olingan dalillar bilan quvvatlaydi. D noto‘g‘ri: matnda Sobirining tarjimai holi berilmagan va obrazlar shunchaki sanab o‘tilmaydi.

passage: In many countries, people who live near a newly opened public park report feeling happier a year later. Some researchers take this as evidence that green space itself improves well-being. Others point out that new parks are often built in neighborhoods that are already becoming wealthier, and rising incomes could explain the change in mood. Economist Shahnoza Valiyeva notes that the two explanations make different predictions: if green space is responsible, residents who rarely visit the park should feel little change, whereas if income is responsible, park visits should matter less than changes in household earnings.
stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
option_a: To argue that new public parks improve the well-being of nearby residents
option_b: To criticize researchers for ignoring the effects of rising incomes
option_c: To present two possible explanations for a finding and identify a way that evidence could distinguish between them
option_d: To show that people who visit parks often earn more than those who do not
explanation_en:
The text describes a finding (residents near new parks feel happier) and two explanations (green space versus rising incomes). Valiyeva then explains how the explanations predict different results, which could be used to tell them apart. The text does not take a side. Choice C states this purpose.

Choice A is wrong because the text presents the green-space view as only one of two explanations and does not endorse it. Choice B uses the wrong verb: the text presents the income explanation as a point some researchers raise, and it does not criticize anyone. Choice D is wrong because the text never compares the incomes of park visitors with those of non-visitors.
explanation_uz:
Matnda bir natija (yangi bog‘ yonida yashovchilar o‘zini baxtliroq his qiladi) va ikki izoh (yashil hudud yoki daromadning oshishi) tasvirlanadi. Keyin Valiyeva bu izohlar turli natijalarni bashorat qilishini va shu orqali ularni bir-biridan ajratish mumkinligini tushuntiradi. Matn hech qaysi tomonni olmaydi. C javob shu maqsadni ifodalaydi.

A noto‘g‘ri: matn yashil hudud qarashini ikki izohdan biri sifatida beradi va uni qo‘llab-quvvatlamaydi. B noto‘g‘ri fe’l ishlatadi: matn daromad izohini ba’zi tadqiqotchilar ko‘targan fikr sifatida keltiradi, hech kimni tanqid qilmaydi. D noto‘g‘ri: matnda bog‘ga boradiganlar va bormaydiganlarning daromadi taqqoslanmaydi.
